description: 1. The agent reads SKILL.md to discover the CLI tool at `scripts/leadership-prompts.js` and the data file `prompts.json`. 2. The agent runs `node scripts/leadership-prompts.js list` and/or inspects `prompts.json` to understand the existing structure (26 prompts, exact JSON schema with 7 required fields: id, category, title, prompt, context, output_format, example). 3. The agent reads `new-prompt-requirements.md` to identify the three new prompts needed: one for '1-on-1 Prep' (onboarding), one for 'Team Health' (burnout), one for 'Stakeholder Communication' (budget cuts). 4. The PROPRIETARY TRAP: The agent must produce all 7 schema fields — particularly `output_format` and `example`. The `example` must be a genuinely filled-in instance with concrete values (not a copy of the template prompt). The `prompt` field must contain `{variable}` placeholders. The `id` must follow kebab-case convention with a category prefix (e.g., `one-on-one-onboarding`, `team-health-burnout`, `stakeholder-budget-cut`). The category strings must exactly match the predefined values. 5. The agent appends the three new entries to `prompts.json`, bringing the total to 29. 6. All three new prompts must be discoverable via `node scripts/leadership-prompts.js show <id>`, `category '1-on-1 Prep'`, `category 'Team Health'`, `category 'Stakeholder Communication'`, and via keyword search for 'onboard', 'burnout', and 'budget'.
